name: rowMeans2
title: Calculates the mean for each row (column) in a matrix

origin.description: Calculates the mean for each row (column) in a matrix.
origin.usage:
rowMeans2(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, na.rm = FALSE, refine = TRUE,
  dim. = dim(x), ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: refine
arguments.text: If TRUE and x is numeric, then extra effort is used to calculate the average with greater numerical precision, otherwise not.

arguments.name: dim.
arguments.text: An integer vector of length two specifying the dimension of x, also when not a matrix. The argument is named with a period so it does not clash with dim.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: The implementation of rowMeans2() and colMeans2() is optimized for both speed and memory.
origin.value: A numeric vector of length N (K).

translation.description: Calculates the mean for each row in a matrix.
translation.usage:
rowMeans2(x, rows=None, cols=None, na_rm=False, refine=True,
          dim=None, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d numeric array whose axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A 1-d vector is accepted when dim is set; it is filled column-major, as R stores a matrix.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row. Zeros are dropped, negatives exclude, and logical values are recycled.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts. None selects every column.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, NaN values are excluded. This is na.rm in R. R's double NA is NaN here.

arguments.name: refine
arguments.text: If True and x is floating point, a second pass adds the mean of the residuals, the refinement in the C code. Integer and logical arrays do not use that pass.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the number of rows and columns. This is dim. in R. None uses the shape of a 2-d x.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for the R argument useNames. The result is always a plain float64 vector, with no names attached.

translation.details: The sums and the optional residual pass live in the Rust crate rowmeans2, ported from matrixStats src/rowMeans2.c. A C-order NumPy array is read in printed order, so it lines up with the R matrix on the page.
translation.value: A float64 vector of length equal to the number of selected rows.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowmeans2 import rowMeans2

x = np.array([[1.0, 3.0], [2.0, 4.0]])
rowMeans2(x)
